five_minutes: ECB keeps euro yields high as Vujčić warns inflation stays above target, adding upside to USD and pressure on INR.
RBI’s ₹25 bn OMO sale adds supply to the 10‑yr G‑sec market, likely nudging Indian yields higher and tightening equity valuations.
BoE holds rates at 3.75% and pauses gilt sales, keeping UK yields steady and limiting capital outflows from India.
RBI’s reverse repo auction absorbed ₹2.25 cr at 5.24% cut‑off, setting a short‑term funding floor for banks.
Japan’s real exports rise 2% supporting yen, which could modestly ease INR pressure via USD/INR dynamics.

theses.thesis: Crypto is rising because markets expect a global recession (crypto trading as the recession hedge)
US policy decisions under Trump are pushing the US economy toward decline, contrary to the stated growth narrative
Gold and silver will NOT rise further even in a recession, because they are already at all-time highs
Nifty 29-Sep futures will fall below 23,000 before expiry

buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: ECB signals slower rate cuts, keeping euro yields elevated
items.what_happened: ECB President Boris Vujčić told Reuters that inflation remains above target and the bank will maintain a cautious stance on monetary easing.
items.why_it_matters: Higher euro yields may attract foreign inflows, pressuring the rupee lower and reducing appetite for emerging‑market assets, including Indian equities.

items.headline: ECB consumer inflation expectations stay elevated, limiting near‑term euro‑zone rate cuts
items.what_happened: The ECB Consumer Expectations Survey for August 2026 showed inflation expectations at 3.2% YoY, above the bank’s 2% target.
items.why_it_matters: Persistently high expectations keep the ECB from cutting rates, supporting a stronger euro and adding pressure on INR via USD/INR dynamics.

items.headline: BoE holds policy rate at 3.75%, signaling no immediate easing
items.what_happened: The Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee kept the Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75% in September 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Stable UK rates keep GBP yields steady, limiting capital outflows from India to the UK and modestly influencing INR via USD/GBP cross‑rates.

items.headline: BoE pauses gilt‑sale programme, curbing upward pressure on UK bond yields
items.what_happened: The Bank of England announced a temporary suspension of Asset Purchase Facility gilt sales while reviewing its selling model.
items.why_it_matters: Yield stabilization in the UK reduces competition for Indian G‑sec yields, supporting demand for Indian sovereigns.

items.headline: BoJ expands climate‑focused funding operations, widening yen‑denominated funding supply
items.what_happened: The Bank of Japan amended the terms of its funds‑supplying operations to increase financing for climate‑change responses.
items.why_it_matters: More yen liquidity can ease funding pressures in the yen market, marginally reducing yen‑INR volatility.

items.headline: Japan’s real exports rise 2% YoY, supporting yen demand
items.what_happened: Japan reported a 2% year‑on‑year increase in real exports for the latest month.
items.why_it_matters: Improved export performance may strengthen the yen, adding downward pressure on INR via USD/INR dynamics.

items.headline: RBI conducts ₹25,000 cr OMO sale, adding supply to the 10‑yr G‑sec market
items.what_happened: The Reserve Bank announced an open‑market operation sale of Government of India securities worth ₹25,000 crore scheduled for 21 September 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Increased supply could lift Indian 10‑year yields, raising the cost of capital and pressuring equity valuations.

items.headline: RBI’s 3‑day reverse repo auction absorbs ₹2.25 cr at 5.24% cut‑off
items.what_happened: The RBI’s variable‑rate reverse repo auction on 18 September 2026 received offers of ₹2.22 cr and accepted ₹2.22 cr at a cut‑off rate of 5.24%.
items.why_it_matters: The repo rate sets a floor for short‑term funding, influencing money‑market rates and banks’ net‑interest margins.

items.headline: Government bond auction clears at 7.23% (2041) and 7.69% (2076), confirming elevated G‑sec yields
items.what_happened: The RBI’s primary dealer auction for government securities resulted in cut‑off yields of 7.2305% for the 2041 bond and 7.6863% for the 2076 bond.
items.why_it_matters: Yield levels set the benchmark for the Indian sovereign curve, influencing G‑sec pricing, fund flows and equity discount rates.

items.headline: Overnight money‑market weighted average rate stays near 4.9%, indicating tight liquidity
items.what_happened: Money‑market data for 17 September showed an overnight weighted average rate of 4.89% across call money and repo segments.
items.why_it_matters: Higher overnight rates raise funding costs for corporates and NBFCs, affecting credit spreads and profitability.

items.headline: RBI initiates review of FEMA circulars, potentially easing foreign‑exchange compliance
items.what_happened: The Reserve Bank issued a circular on 8 September 2026 announcing a review of existing FEMA regulations.
items.why_it_matters: Regulatory easing could improve FII/FPI entry, supporting rupee stability and equity inflows.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.
